description: Table 5 is a single rendered data table (no plots or micrographs) tabulating Williamson-Hall style X-ray line-profile parameters for austenite in two Nb-microalloyed low-density steels. The header rows give "Peaks" and "Aging states", then two super-columns, "0.02Nb" and "0.04Nb", each subdivided into four identical sub-columns labelled "Θ" (theta, printed with an uppercase theta glyph), "β", "βcosθ" and "4sinθ". Twelve data rows are grouped by three austenite reflections — (111), (200) and (220) — each with four aging states: as-cast, 723 K, 773 K and 823 K. The table therefore contains 3 peaks × 4 aging states × 2 alloys × 4 parameters = 96 numeric cells. Values are printed to three decimals; Θ ranges roughly from 21.192 to 36.303, β from 0.373 to 0.691, βcosθ from 0.348 to 0.557, and 4sinθ from 1.446 to 2.368, with 4sinθ varying only with the reflection (peak position) and not with alloy or aging state. The tabulated βcosθ and 4sinθ pairs are the raw inputs for the βcosθ–4sinθ linear fit whose slope yields the microstrain ε; the figure's argument is that these line-broadening data feed the dislocation-density and dislocation-strengthening calculation reported downstream. No error bars, uncertainties, or fits are shown — only the raw tabulated values.

subfigures.description: A single 12-row data table listing θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ for the (111), (200) and (220) austenite reflections of 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels in the as-cast, 723 K, 773 K and 823 K aging states.

observations.observation: Table 5 lists four XRD line-profile parameters — Θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ — for austenite in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, each alloy occupying its own four sub-columns.
The table is organised by three austenite peaks, printed as (111), (200) and (220), each with four aging states: as-cast, 723 K, 773 K and 823 K.

For the (111) reflection of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel, Θ = 21.242, β = 0.409, βcosθ = 0.381 and 4sinθ = 1.449; for the as-cast 0.04Nb steel the same reflection gives β = 0.373, βcosθ = 0.348 and 4sinθ = 1.449.
For the (200) reflection, βcosθ of the as-cast state is 0.525 in 0.02Nb and 0.550 in 0.04Nb, and rises to 0.553 (0.02Nb) and 0.520 (0.04Nb) after aging at 823 K.

For the (220) reflection of 0.04Nb, β decreases monotonically with increasing aging temperature, from 0.691 (as-cast) to 0.642 (723 K), 0.604 (773 K) and 0.601 (823 K); βcosθ falls correspondingly from 0.557 to 0.485.
For the (220) reflection of 0.02Nb, β decreases from 0.637 (as-cast) to 0.630 (723 K), 0.601 (773 K) and 0.560 (823 K), while βcosθ falls from 0.514 to 0.451.
The printed 4sinθ values depend only on the reflection and are essentially invariant across alloy and aging state: about 1.446-1.451 for (111), 1.662-1.667 for (200) and 2.364-2.368 for (220).
The tabulated Θ values lie between 21.192 and 21.267 for (111), between 24.552 and 24.628 for (200), and between 36.228 and 36.303 for (220).
No uncertainties, error bars, fitted slope, or R² value are printed anywhere in the table; only raw three-decimal values are given.
The caption states the table gives the values of θ, β, βcosθ, and 4sinθ for austenite in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.

The citing text states that ε is calculated from the slope of the linear fitting graph of βcosθ–4sinθ, and that the corresponding θ, β, βcosθ and 4sinθ values for austenite in the 0.02Nb steel are recorded in Table 5.

The citing text states that dislocation strengthening in austenite of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel is 113.1 MPa, falling to 87.4, 70.8 and 40.2 MPa after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K, respectively; these values are not printed in the table itself.
The citing text states that dislocation strengthening in austenite of the 0.04Nb steel is 169.8 MPa as-cast and 129.0, 106.1 and 98.9 MPa after aging at 723, 773 and 823 K, respectively.

measured_quantities: microstrain ε (from βcosθ–4sinθ slope, per citing text)
unreadable_items: The header symbol is printed as an uppercase Θ in the table while the caption uses θ — treated as the same diffraction angle; no values are illegible
Table has no units row, so the unit of Θ (degrees) and of β are inferred from context rather than printed
